The core mechanism involves predicting a continuous scalar field $s: \mathbb{R}^3 \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ instead of a density $\sigma(\mathbf{x})$ [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that 'In SDF-based neural fields, instead of predicting a density 𝜎(x) directly, the network predicts an SDF value 𝑠(x)' and defines the SDF as 'a continuous scalar field 𝑠 : R3 → R'. This directly supports the claim that the core mechanism involves predicting a continuous scalar field instead of a density.
supported
This approach addresses the geometric inaccuracy and surface holes typical of density-based NeRFs by leveraging the zero-level set of the SDF to define geometry [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the approach addresses geometric inaccuracy and surface holes by leveraging the zero-level set of the SDF. Source [S1] explicitly mentions that combining NeRF with SDFs provides a 'more explicit and smooth formulation of surfaces' (addressing the issues) and formally defines the surface as the 'zero-level set {x | s(x) = 0}'. Therefore, all facts in the claim are present in the evidence.
supported

This matches the claim exactly.
